summary: While retiring model self-certification in favor of hook-observed episode tracking is a sound architectural improvement, critical edge cases in directory resolution, legacy sentinel coexistence, and session state updates cause silent reconnaissance lockouts and improper planning lifecycle classifications. Specifically, skill-scoped execution bypasses root directory resolution when running from subdirectories, legacy pending sentinels override valid episode records, and existing episode states fail to update their session ID when asked clarifying questions in new sessions.

findings.title: Skill-scoped episode phase recorder bypasses project root resolution in subdirectories
findings.body: In `hooks/episode-phase.ts`, `cwd` is set to `start` whenever `argWorkflow` is present (`const cwd = argWorkflow ? start : governedRoot(start)`). When an `AskUserQuestion` tool executes from a subdirectory within a governed project (e.g. `/repo/src`), `episode-phase.ts` writes `.planning/.state/episode.json` inside the subdirectory (`/repo/src/.planning/.state/episode.json`) rather than walking up to the project root (`/repo`). Because guards and lifecycle classifiers inspect the project root, the recorded clarification phase is ignored, leaving reconnaissance permanently blocked for subdirectory invocations.
findings.recommendation: Resolve `cwd` using `governedRoot(start) ?? start` so that marked or existing project roots are always preferred over the process working directory, even when `argWorkflow` is specified.

findings.title: Pending legacy sentinels short-circuit and invalidate valid episode state checks
findings.body: In `workflows/lib/approved-artifact.ts`, `hasOnlyBenignPreplanState` computes `episodeIsBenign` but immediately returns the evaluation of any existing sentinel file if `sentinel.length === 1`. If a project upgraded from a previous version where `.planning/DEV_CLARIFIED.json` was written with `{"status":"pending"}` upon skill entry, `episodeIsBenign` evaluates to `true` after `AskUserQuestion` records `episode.json`. However, `if (sentinel.length === 1)` evaluates `value.status === "clarified"` against the pending sentinel, returns `false`, and never reaches `return episodeIsBenign`. This misclassifies a validly clarified project as `blocked`.
findings.recommendation: Allow `hasOnlyBenignPreplanState` to return `true` if `episodeIsBenign` is `true`, regardless of whether an un-updated legacy sentinel file is present on disk.

findings.title: Session ID is not updated on existing episode state when clarified in a new session
findings.body: In `hooks/episode-phase.ts`, `base` is initialized as `existing ?? initEpisodeState({ workflow, sessionId })`. If `episode.json` already exists from a previous session S1, `existing` is reused without updating `existing.sessionId` to `payload.session_id` (S2). When `clarify-before-recon-guard.ts` subsequently runs in session S2, `clarified()` checks `value.sessionId === payload.session_id`. Because `value.sessionId` remains set to S1, the check fails and denies reconnaissance despite `AskUserQuestion` having been called in session S2.
findings.recommendation: Update `base.sessionId` to the current `sessionId` when `payload.session_id` is present, or update `clarify-before-recon-guard.ts` to accept valid clarification phases recorded for active sessions.
